title: Make Classroom Management Your Top Priority https://smartclassroommanagement.com/2009/07/25/make-classroom-management-your-top-priority/
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Linsin opens with an extended anecdote about fixing a stuck sliding screen door: adjusting the wheel tension made no real difference, but a squirt of WD-40 solved the problem instantly, and he uses this as a metaphor for classroom management. He argues that effective classroom management functions the same way as the grease -- everything about teaching becomes easier with it, while its absence makes even the loftiest academic goals harder to reach. He connects on-task time directly to learning outcomes, arguing that a year's worth of small interruptions can add up to hundreds of lost instructional hours and measurably harm academic progress. He also links classroom management to teacher well-being, contending that it is the leading reason so many teachers leave the profession, and that teachers who prioritize it are the least stressed and most satisfied. To illustrate, he describes three teacher types observable at whole-school assemblies: the anxious 'Corrector,' the resigned 'Ignorer,' and the calm, trusting 'Expert' whose classroom management plan does the work for her. The piece closes by urging teachers to see classroom management not as one task among many but as the top priority that makes every other goal possible.
points: Classroom management is compared to WD-40: it doesn't add the goal itself, but it removes the friction that makes every other part of teaching difficult.
The amount of time students spend on-task, more than any other factor, determines learning outcomes, and lost time from interruptions compounds into hundreds of hours over a school year.
Poor classroom management is identified as the primary reason teachers leave the profession, while strong management correlates with lower stress and higher job satisfaction.
Three observable teacher types at school assemblies -- the Corrector, the Ignorer, and the Expert -- illustrate how differently teachers experience stress based on their classroom management skill.
Making classroom management the top priority, above content delivery itself, is presented as the precondition for reaching the 'loftiest goal' of inspiring academic growth.
quotes: Effective classroom management works like WD-40. With it, everything is easier. The inverse is also true; without effective classroom management, everything about teaching is made more difficult.
The loftiest goal for a teacher is to inspire life-changing academic growth in each of his or her students. But to realize this goal, classroom management must be the top priority.

The amount of time your students spend on-task and attentive trumps all else when it comes to learning. So whenever they’re off-task, or whenever you’re interrupted during a lesson, learning is adversely affected.
Poor classroom management is the primary reason—by a long shot—why so many teachers leave the profession. Stressed-out, burned-out, and unhappy teachers are on every campus.
The Expert – She is relaxed and able to enjoy the event because classroom management is her top priority. She knows her students will behave as expected and trusts in her classroom management plan.
Like the expert in this example, teachers with effective classroom management skills have a lot less to concern themselves with.
